docs.getting-started.content:
Getting started
The overview of MELOPHOS and the quickstart for running the stack on your own machine.
Start here if this is your first visit.
Quickstart: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/README.md>

docs.instruments.content:
Instruments
How instrument profiles work and how to align the lights to your keyboard or guitar.
If your instrument is missing, a new profile is the easiest first contribution.
Instruments guide: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/docs/instruments.md>

docs.integrations.content:
Integrations
Spotify, WLED, Home Assistant and webhooks.
Each one is optional and off until you turn it on.
Integrations: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/docs/integrations.md>

docs.protocol.content:
Protocol
The messages the hub and the server send to each other.
Useful if you are building a client or a tool that talks to the hub.
Protocol: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/docs/protocol.md>

docs.roadmap.content:
Roadmap
What is built and what is planned across the three versions.
Dates are targets and not promises.
Roadmap: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/docs/roadmap.md>

docs.self-hosting.content:
Self-hosting
How to run the MELOPHOS server stack on your own computer.
MELOPHOS has no hosted service, so everything runs at home.
Self-hosting guide: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/docs/self-hosting.md>

docs.song-import.content:
Song import
How songs come into MELOPHOS and what formats we read.
Share only your own playing and your own arrangements.
Song import: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/docs/song-import.md>

faq.keyboard-not-detected.content:
The keyboard is not detected
The hub reads the 3.5 mm MIDI jack today. USB-MIDI and Bluetooth MIDI are still to come.
Check the keyboard on a computer first because some only take power through USB. If nothing appears there then use the MIDI jacks or the audio input.
Support page: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/SUPPORT.md>

faq.lights-drift.content:
The lights drift out of line
The profile's LED spacing does not match the bar or strip you use.
The alignment section of the instruments guide explains how to fix it.
Support page: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/SUPPORT.md>
Instruments guide: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/docs/instruments.md>

faq.studio-no-midi.content:
Studio cannot see a MIDI device
WebMIDI needs a secure address (https or localhost) and a browser that supports it: Chrome or Edge or Firefox 108 and later.
Safari does not support WebMIDI. Web Bluetooth works in Chrome and Edge only.
Support page: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/SUPPORT.md>

hardware.enclosures.content:
Enclosures
Printable parts for the hub and the light bars.
Most are planned and not yet finished.
Enclosure notes: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/hardware/enclosures/README.md>

hardware.fret-bar.content:
Fret bar
A flexible LED grid with one LED for each string at each fret.
It is planned for version 3 with the guitar profiles.
Fret bar notes: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/hardware/frets/README.md>

hardware.hub.content:
Hub
The board that reads notes from the instrument and drives the light bars.
Check the Rev A requirements before you order parts.
Hub notes: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/hardware/hub/README.md>
Parts list: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/hardware/bom/hub-rev-a.csv>

hardware.key-bars.content:
Key bars
A strip of 12 LEDs for one octave with one LED for every key.
Bars join end to end along the keyboard.
Octave bar notes: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/hardware/keys-octave/README.md>
Parts list: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/blob/main/hardware/bom/README.md>

mod.guide.raid.content:
A raid
1. Time out the accounts that are posting. Do not argue with them.
2. Tell the owner in moderator-only. If the owner is away, a Maintainer starts banning.
3. The owner pauses invites and direct messages.
4. Delete what was posted. Leave the entries in mod-log.
5. When it is quiet, the owner raises the verification level for a day and writes two lines in moderator-only on what happened.

mod.guide.report.content:
A member report
1. Read the link first. The link is the evidence. The words under Why are the reporter's own and are not verified.
2. Open a thread on the entry in mod-log.
3. Say in the thread what you did.
4. React with a tick when it is done.
5. A report about a member of staff arrives by email, so tell the owner.

mod.guide.security.content:
A security post
1. Delete the message if it gives detail.
2. Post /mod reply with the security template.
3. Never ask for detail in public or in a direct message.
4. Tell a Maintainer in moderator-only.

mod.guide.timeout.content:
A timeout
1. Remind first. A timeout is for repeat or serious breaks of the rules.
2. Use the shortest timeout that stops the harm.
3. Write what you did and why in moderator-only.
4. A Moderator cannot act on a Maintainer. Pass it on.

mod.reply.be-kind.content: From the moderators: Please keep the tone kind and patient. Our Code of Conduct applies everywhere in this server.

mod.reply.english.content: From the moderators: Please write in English in the public channels so that everyone can follow, moderators included.

mod.reply.needs-details.content: From the moderators: We need more detail to help. Please add what you were trying to do, the version you run, how you run it and the exact error as text in a code block.

mod.reply.no-direct-messages.content: From the moderators: Please ask in public and not by direct message. The answer then helps the next person. We never ask for a password, a key or money in a direct message.

mod.reply.one-topic.content: From the moderators: Please keep one question in each post. Open a new post for the next question so that each answer is easy to find.

mod.reply.search-first.content: From the moderators: Please search this forum and the documentation first. The /docs and /faq commands can help. If you cannot find an answer, post again and say what you tried.

mod.reply.security.content: From the moderators: Please do not share the details of a security problem here or in a direct message. Report it privately instead: type /security to see how. We never take reports by direct message.

static.bug.content:
Open a new issue on GitHub and pick the form that fits: a bug, a feature, a hardware problem or a docs problem.
1. Search the open issues in case we already know about it.
2. Say what you did, what you expected and what happened instead.
3. Add the version you run and what hardware you use (hub revision, instrument model and how it connects) and the exact error as text.
4. Leave out passwords and keys.
A security problem never goes in an issue. Type /security instead.
Issue forms: <https://github.com/melophos/melophos/issues/new/choose>
